text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein meets Jordanian participants in the Copenhagen forum for Arab-Israeli peace, monarch says throws his weight with any effort that supports the peace process and "consolidates its foundations".
- The government plans to abolish 125 village councils and merge them with nearby municaplities as part of a government drive to improve services in rural areas.

- Judicial sources say detainees who were granted amnesty under a royal pardon may be released on Thursday or Friday, but the pardon excludes those arrested on charges relating to drugs, rape and membership of illegal underground groups.
- Leading Islamist deputy Akaylah, who is in favour of Islamist participation in cabinet, says distance from the centre of decision-making means isolating the movement.

- Justice minister assures a delegation of relatives of detained Jordanians in Kuwaiti prisons that their conditions are satisfactory; says government is satisfied by the report of the Omani and Qatari ambassadors who met the inmates in Kuwait and spoke to them about their conditions.

- The Amman Financial Market enters the recovery stage; stocks rise to their highest level for over a year in reaction to parliament's scrapping of a 15 percent tax on companies raising their capital.
- Crown Prince Hassan to leave on Thursday to Britain on a private visit followed by an official programme in France to include meetings with top French leaders.
- Prime Minister Kabariti, Islamists in dialogue over coaltion, but outcome remains unpredictable.
- King urges university presidents to upgrade education.
- British foreign secretary's special envoy Chaplin arrives to discuss Middle East cooperation.
